title: Reviewing Regulatory Framework for Integrated Shield Plans and Assessing Practice of Pre-authorisation
what_it_is: Reviewing Regulatory Framework for Integrated Shield Plans and Assessing Practice of Pre-authorisation

sections.label: Integrated Shield Plan regulation questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the Government will review Integrated Shield Plan regulation, address rising costs and premiums, and protect policyholders from insurer changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health given Integrated Shield Plans are primarily healthcare financing tools, whether the Government will consider reviewing the regulatory framework for Integrated Shield Plans to give greater regulatory oversight to the Ministry, or adopting a stronger dual or co-regulation model, to ensure better alignment with national healthcare priorities and patient protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health what are the measures the Ministry intends to take to address the issues of escalating private healthcare costs, insurance premiums and insurers refusing pre-authorisation certificates at certain hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health given that pre-authorisation helps ensure that policyholders have access to non-panel doctors and receive cost-effective treatments, whether the Ministry will implement measures to ensure that policyholders continue to have access to the full benefits of their Integrated Shield Plan should an insurer stop issuing pre-authorisation certificates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health given recent unilateral changes by Integrated Shield Plan insurers, such as new pre-authorisation rules for existing policyholders (a) whether the Government will consider a dedicated healthcare insurance law to protect consumers and establish a mandatory dispute resolution platform; and (b) whether there are regulations to prevent insurers from influencing healthcare decisions against policyholders’ best interests.

sections.label: Rider claims likelihood and size
sections.summary: A patient with a private hospital rider is 1.4 times likelier to claim, and claims average about 1.4 times larger.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The likelihood of a patient with a private hospital rider making a claim is 1.4 times that of a patient without a rider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The size of the claim is also on average about 1.4 times that of a patient without a rider.

sections.label: Insurer health portfolio losses
sections.summary: Insurers are making losses or barely breaking even on health portfolios due to excessive competition, described as market failure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Here, insurers are either making losses or barely breaking even on their health portfolios.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The situation is due to excessive competition that has gone wrong – another type of market failure.

sections.label: MOH cost and consumer measures
sections.summary: MOH published over 2,800 doctor fee benchmarks, will educate consumers, study guiding private hospital fees, and work through the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Insurers will need to balance between providing assurance and protection, and encouraging prudent consumption and servicing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will do more to educate consumers on choosing the appropriate health insurance coverage for their needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To rein in private sector cost increases, MOH has developed and published over 2,800 doctor fee benchmarks, which providers and insurers reference to set fees and review reimbursements respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will study what more can be done to guide fee setting by private hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MOH will also continue to work through the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee, which brings together key stakeholders from healthcare providers, medical professionals, insurers and consumer representatives, to address these issues collaboratively.

sections.label: Insurer performance data publication
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Ministry will publish insurer performance data such as approval rates, turnaround times and appeal outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And secondly, some of these residents have also asked me if an insurer delays or rejects a pre-authorisation without good reason, what recourse do they have?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And I hear from the Minister of State that fee benchmarks are being published, but will the Ministry also consider publishing data on insurer performance, such as approval rates, turnaround times, appeal outcomes, so that Singaporeans can see whether insurers are acting in their best interests?

sections.label: Reasons for claim rejections
sections.summary: Rejections typically occur because of contract exclusions, fees being too high, or treatment plans being too aggressive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: What we hear, what we understand is that, typically if there are rejections, it is possibly because there is an exclusion in the original contract, so you could not have gotten it covered anyway, or the fees are too high, the treatment plan may be too aggressive, meaning you have not considered other treatment plans.

sections.label: Fee benchmarks for hospital charges
sections.summary: MOH discusses engagements with insurers on product design and is studying benchmarks for hospital charges beyond professional fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Our conversations, discussions and engagements with insurers on their insurance product design is one, but we are also looking at different elements, including introducing fee benchmarks which we have done since 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have introduced benchmarks for private professional fees and this guides the pricing and guards against overcharging.
We are now studying the possibility of going beyond professional fees, by introducing more benchmarks for hospital charges to guide fee setting by private hospitals.

sections.label: MediSave levers on IPs
sections.summary: For IPs, MediSave is used as part of payment, giving levers to ensure compliance with required parameters on riders and co-payments.

sentences.text: For IPs, for example, they tap on MediSave as part of the payment and so, we have levers to make sure that they comply with the different parameters that we require of them, in terms of riders, in terms of co-payments.

sections.label: MOH and MAS regulatory oversight
sections.summary: MOH and MAS work closely to exercise regulatory oversight so IP insurers protect policyholders and their products are sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, that is how the system works and in a way, it is a mechanism for the insurers to manage their costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, on MOH and MAS' part, we work closely to exercise regulatory oversight so that IP insurers protect the interests of policyholders and that their products are sustainable.

sections.label: Notification of terms changes
sections.summary: There is a requirement for notification if insurers change their terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To also allay the Member's concerns, there is a requirement for notification if they change their terms and conditions.

sections.label: Patient protection versus insurance profits
sections.summary: A question asks how MOH ensures patient protection is at the heart of the regulatory framework rather than insurance profits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And now they see premiums rising and they are facing more exclusions and tighter panels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, how is MOH ensuring that patient protection actually is at the heart of the regulatory framework rather than insurance profits?

sections.label: Statutory powers over private IPs
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOH is considering stronger statutory powers over the private portion of IPs to better protect patients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And related to that, MediShield Life is tightly regulated by law, so a lot of basic IP protections are there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But is MOH considering stronger statutory powers over the private portion of IPs to better protect patients?

sections.label: Fee benchmarks against overcharging
sections.summary: Benchmarks on fees are being introduced to protect against overcharging and guide pricing, relating to amounts charged versus claimed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Separately, we are also putting in benchmarks, fee benchmarks, to protect against overcharging and guide the pricing, because it is also about how much is charged versus how much they are going to claim.

sections.label: Benchmark details not available
sections.summary: The Member asked about the benchmarks mentioned earlier, but no details are available at this juncture, though professional fee benchmarks exist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Member had asked specifically about the benchmarks that I mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I do not have details at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We already have benchmarks on the professional fees.
